body:
Quiet day, no crossings. The scanner found zero arbitrage opportunities across the 73 live contracts it checked on Kalshi and Polymarket. That's the normal state of affairs — most scans turn up nothing, and today's price grid, while busy, is internally consistent rather than mispriced.

Gold itself is in the middle of a strong run: spot was quoted around $4,414–$4,420 on August 17, 2026, up sharply from roughly $4,070 just two weeks earlier and from about $3,400 a year ago. That rally shows up cleanly in the contract pricing: Kalshi's settle above $4,011.99 contract for August 31, 2026 trades at 96–98 cents, essentially priced as a near-certainty since spot is already $400 above that line, while the above $4,411.99 strike — right at today's spot — sits near a coin flip at 46–51 cents. Polymarket's weekly touch contracts tell the same story from a different angle: touch high $4,450 for the week of August 17 is bid 62–65 cents and touch low $4,350 is bid 63–69 cents, both elevated simply because current spot sits between those two levels and gold is volatile enough to plausibly poke through either side before the week closes.

Worth noting for readers unfamiliar with the mechanics: Kalshi's gold contracts settle against a price snapshot at a fixed date and time, while Polymarket's touch contracts pay out if the price crosses the level at any point during the window — a materially different bar that naturally produces different-looking probabilities for similar strikes without implying any tradeable gap. Several of today's Kalshi strikes also show zero 24-hour volume, a reminder that a wide-looking quote on a thin book isn't the same as an executable opportunity.
headline: Gold scan finds no arbitrage across 73 contracts as rally to $4,414 prices consistently
